decision_conditions: The Council does not consider that the grounds specified by the applicant/agent sufficient reason to justify the proposed removal of a mature tree which makes a positive contribution to the amenity of the locality and wider borough.a)	A full investigative report is required to substantiate claims that the tree is the cause of subsidence. b)	Pruning of branches to provide clearance of the roof, thus removing physical contact of branches with the roof, upon the advice of a qualified arboriculturist, would be considered, should a further application be made for this. Under common law you can prune any branches which are encroaching over the boundary, and must offer the cut branches back to the tree owner. If this pruning involves any cutting beyond the boundary, consent must be gained from the tree owner at no. 40. In either case, an application would have to be made and consent granted by the council before works could take place.c)	Shading issues in the garden could be addressed by making an application for crown thinning or crown reduction, after consulting with a qualified arboriculturist. If this pruning involves any cutting beyond the boundary, consent must be gained from the tree owner at no. 40.  d)	Solutions are available for guttering systems/vents/drains which prevent them becoming blocked by annual leaf/acorn drop.
